Chapter 8: Navigating Relapses and Setbacks with Compassion.
No journey of change goes perfectly, does it? There’ll always be bumps along the road. Maybe you notice those old patterns—people-pleasing, rescuing, or even putting your own needs last—sneaking back in, especially when life gets stressful or uncertain.
But here’s something really important: those moments aren’t failures. They’re actually chances to learn and grow. Think about it like learning to ride a bike. You fall, sure, but each time you get back up, you’re building skill and confidence. The real trick is meeting setbacks with compassion, not criticism.
So when you notice a slip, try pausing and asking yourself—what triggered that old behavior? Was it fear, loneliness, or maybe wanting someone’s approval? What need were you hoping to fill? Instead of blaming yourself, get curious. You can learn so much by exploring what’s underneath those moments.
Here are a few gentle ways to move through setbacks:
First, acknowledge what happened without judging yourself harshly. Then, consider reaching out to a friend, a support group, or a therapist—sometimes a fresh perspective helps more than you think. Take a look at what’s worked for you in the past, and maybe brainstorm what you might do differently next time. And finally, recommit to taking care of yourself and setting healthy boundaries, even in small ways. Every little bit counts.
Setbacks can even be a sign that you’re facing new challenges or growth opportunities. Maybe a relationship is shifting, or it’s time to be more honest—with yourself or others. If you can stay present and approach yourself with kindness, these moments can actually deepen your resilience and understanding.
So, here’s the key takeaway: progress isn’t about being perfect. It’s about your willingness to keep moving forward. Every time you come back to self-awareness and self-care, no matter how small the step, that’s a victory worth celebrating.
